horizontal_press.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

incline_press.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

decline_press.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

vertical_press.summary: Shoulder-press EMG directly supports anterior/medial deltoid and triceps involvement across seated/standing and barbell/dumbbell variants.

horizontal_press_triceps_bias.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

dip_chest_bias.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

dip_triceps_bias.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

horizontal_pull.summary: Direct row-family EMG evidence across inverted, prone/barbell and suspension rows supports latissimus dorsi and mid/lower trapezius as major back contributors, with biceps and posterior deltoid also substantially recruited. DB++ retains biceps and shoulders as indirect because their relative contribution varies materially by row variant.

vertical_pull.summary: Direct pull-up EMG evidence supports latissimus dorsi and biceps as major contributors, with posterior shoulder and mid-trapezius involvement; this directly supports the vertical-pull family.

shrug.summary: A standardized resistance-training EMG study directly measured reverse fly and shrug recruitment of deltoid/trapezius regions.

reverse_fly.summary: A standardized resistance-training EMG study directly measured reverse fly and shrug recruitment of deltoid/trapezius regions.

shoulder_abduction.summary: Resistance-exercise EMG directly supports deltoid recruitment in lateral/front raise families; lateral raises emphasize shoulder musculature and front raises emphasize anterior deltoid.

shoulder_external_rotation.summary: Intramuscular/surface EMG directly supports infraspinatus and teres-minor as principal external rotators, with deltoid/scapular muscles contributing by position.

elbow_flexion.summary: Curl studies directly support biceps brachii as a prime elbow flexor across dumbbell, straight-bar and EZ-bar variants.

elbow_flexion_brachioradialis_bias.summary: Curl-variant EMG directly supports substantial brachioradialis involvement and grip-dependent changes in elbow-flexor recruitment.

elbow_extension.summary: Direct EMG evidence supports long- and lateral-head triceps recruitment during loaded elbow-extension exercises.

wrist_flexion.summary: Rule is biomechanically plausible but has not yet been assigned targeted pattern-level literature in DB++.

wrist_extension.summary: Rule is biomechanically plausible but has not yet been assigned targeted pattern-level literature in DB++.

squat.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports high gluteus-maximus activation across squats, lunges, step-ups and related loaded lower-body movements; quadriceps dominance is also well established in squat-family work.

squat_quad_bias.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports high gluteus-maximus activation across squats, lunges, step-ups and related loaded lower-body movements; quadriceps dominance is also well established in squat-family work.

lunge.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports high gluteus-maximus activation across squats, lunges, step-ups and related loaded lower-body movements; quadriceps dominance is also well established in squat-family work.

step_up.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports high gluteus-maximus activation across squats, lunges, step-ups and related loaded lower-body movements; quadriceps dominance is also well established in squat-family work.

knee_extension.summary: Longitudinal resistance-training studies show knee-extension training produces quadriceps hypertrophy, directly supporting quadriceps as the target muscle group.

knee_flexion.summary: Direct EMG evidence supports hamstring activation across leg curl, GHR, good morning and RDL variants.

hip_hinge.summary: Deadlift systematic review supports substantial quadriceps, erector-spinae, gluteal and hamstring activation, with variant-specific differences.

hip_extension.summary: Hip-thrust and hamstring exercise literature supports strong gluteal/hamstring contribution with variant-specific erector-spinae involvement.

glute_ham_raise.summary: Hip-thrust and hamstring exercise literature supports strong gluteal/hamstring contribution with variant-specific erector-spinae involvement.

rack_pull.summary: Deadlift systematic review supports substantial quadriceps, erector-spinae, gluteal and hamstring activation, with variant-specific differences.

anti_rotation.summary: Pallof-press research directly establishes a laterally loaded lumbopelvic postural-control task; related trunk-stabilization literature supports abdominal recruitment, but exact direct/indirect set roles remain an extrapolation.

hip_abduction.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports gluteal activation in hip-abduction/external-rotation exercise families; adduction mapping remains primarily anatomical.

hip_adduction.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports gluteal activation in hip-abduction/external-rotation exercise families; adduction mapping remains primarily anatomical.

plantar_flexion_straight_knee.summary: Standing/knee-extended calf-raise training produces gastrocnemius and soleus hypertrophy; EMG studies confirm triceps-surae recruitment during plantar flexion.

leg_press.summary: Systematic-review evidence supports high gluteus-maximus activation across squats, lunges, step-ups and related loaded lower-body movements; quadriceps dominance is also well established in squat-family work.

conventional_deadlift.summary: Deadlift systematic review supports substantial quadriceps, erector-spinae, gluteal and hamstring activation, with variant-specific differences.

sumo_deadlift.summary: Deadlift systematic review supports substantial quadriceps, erector-spinae, gluteal and hamstring activation, with variant-specific differences.

chest_fly.summary: Bench-press literature supports pectoralis major and triceps as major prime movers with anterior deltoid contribution; inclination changes relative contribution.

pullover.summary: Direct barbell-pullover EMG demonstrates pectoralis-major and latissimus-dorsi recruitment, with pectoralis activation exceeding latissimus in the tested setup.

upright_row.summary: Direct upright-row EMG demonstrates deltoid and trapezius recruitment, with grip width altering relative activation.

face_pull.summary: No exact face-pull study was located in this pass; the mapping is supported indirectly by closely related external-rotation, reverse-fly and upper-back/shoulder EMG evidence.

shoulder_flexion.summary: Resistance-exercise EMG directly supports deltoid recruitment in lateral/front raise families; lateral raises emphasize shoulder musculature and front raises emphasize anterior deltoid.

shoulder_internal_rotation.summary: EMG directly supports subscapularis as a major internal rotator, with arm position strongly affecting selective activation.

hip_flexion.summary: A systematic review and fine-wire EMG evidence directly support iliopsoas and related hip-flexor recruitment during leg raises and loaded hip-flexion tasks.

plantar_flexion_bent_knee.summary: Seated/bent-knee calf raises directly load the triceps surae, with comparatively greater soleus emphasis than straight-leg calf raising.

dorsiflexion.summary: Rule is biomechanically plausible but has not yet been assigned targeted pattern-level literature in DB++.

anti_extension.summary: Prone bridge/plank and rollout-style stabilization studies directly demonstrate substantial rectus-abdominis and oblique activation under anti-extension demands.

lateral_flexion.summary: Side-bridge/lateral-trunk EMG studies directly demonstrate high internal/external oblique and abdominal recruitment.

farmer_carry.summary: Strongman EMG/biomechanics directly included the farmer's walk and documents substantial whole-body, hip and trunk loading; DB++ role labels summarize the event.

loaded_carry.summary: Strongman EMG/biomechanics directly studied farmer, suitcase, keg and yoke-style carries and demonstrates large torso/hip stabilization demands.

sled_push.summary: Direct sled-push EMG shows lower-limb loading, with increasing resistance increasing vastus-lateralis and gastrocnemius activity.

sled_pull.summary: Direct sled-push evidence supports resisted locomotor lower-limb loading, while strongman carry/drag biomechanics support the whole-body loading context; exact backward-pull muscle weighting remains extrapolated.

kettlebell_swing.summary: Kettlebell EMG/biomechanics literature supports whole-body ballistic loading with strong hip-extensor and trunk demands; exact set-credit roles remain model abstractions.

olympic_clean_pull.summary: Olympic-lift literature supports rapid coordinated hip/knee/ankle extension and substantial lower-body/trapezius involvement; DB++ direct/indirect labels remain whole-exercise bookkeeping abstractions across phases.

trunk_flexion.summary: Loaded crunch and sit/curl-up EMG studies directly support rectus abdominis and oblique recruitment during trunk-flexion exercise.

trunk_extension.summary: Roman-chair and machine back-extension EMG directly supports erector-spinae loading with meaningful gluteal and hamstring contribution depending on technique.

trunk_rotation.summary: Rotational training increases internal/external oblique thickness, and flexion-rotation EMG directly demonstrates rectus-abdominis and internal-oblique loading.

neck_flexion.summary: Isometric cervical EMG studies directly support neck-flexor recruitment during resisted flexion.

neck_extension.summary: Isometric cervical EMG studies directly support posterior neck-muscle recruitment during resisted extension.

forearm_pronation.summary: Direct EMG evidence supports pronator quadratus and pronator teres recruitment during resisted forearm pronation.

forearm_supination.summary: Direct EMG evidence supports supinator and load-dependent biceps recruitment during resisted forearm supination.

grip.summary: Direct handgrip EMG studies support substantial forearm flexor/extensor recruitment during loaded gripping and pinching tasks.
